assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Base
items.clue: A substance that neutralises an acid to give a salt and water.

items.label: Hydroxide ion, OH⁻
items.clue: The ion present in aqueous solutions of alkalis; it is what makes a solution alkaline.

items.label: Hydrogen ion, H⁺
items.clue: The ion that all acids produce in aqueous solution; it is what makes a solution acidic.

items.label: Burette
items.clue: The graduated tube that delivers the solution added a little at a time, read to the nearest 0.05 cm³.

questions.stem: Which equation correctly represents the reaction of zinc with dilute sulfuric acid?
questions.explanation: Sulfuric acid produces sulfates and the hydrogen is released as H₂. The equation is balanced as written.

questions.stem: Copper(II) oxide is added to warm dilute sulfuric acid. What is produced?
questions.explanation: A metal oxide is a base, and acids are neutralised by bases to produce a salt and water only.

questions.stem: Calcium carbonate chips are dropped into dilute nitric acid and the mixture fizzes. What are the three products?

options.text: Calcium nitrate and water, no gas
Calcium nitrate, water and carbon dioxide
Calcium nitrite, water and CO₂ gas

questions.explanation: Metal carbonates neutralise acids to produce a salt, water and carbon dioxide; nitric acid produces nitrates.

questions.stem: Which substance is correctly described as an alkali?

options.text: Copper(II) oxide, which is an insoluble base
Copper hydroxide, which will not dissolve
Sodium hydroxide, a soluble metal hydroxide

questions.explanation: An alkali is a base that dissolves in water, so a soluble metal hydroxide such as sodium hydroxide is an alkali.

questions.stem: Which statement about the salts made by acids is correct?
questions.explanation: The acid used decides the salt: hydrochloric acid produces chlorides, nitric acid nitrates and sulfuric acid sulfates.

questions.stem: Which pair of reactants would produce the salt potassium sulfate, K₂SO₄?

options.text: Nitric acid and potassium hydroxide solution
Sulfuric acid and sodium hydroxide solution

questions.explanation: The acid supplies the sulfate ion and the alkali supplies the potassium ions, giving K₂SO₄ and water.

questions.stem: In a reaction between an acid and a base, where does the positive ion in the salt come from?

options.text: From the acid that is being used
From the water formed in the reaction
From the indicator that has been added
From the base, alkali or carbonate used

questions.explanation: The acid supplies the negative ion of the salt and the base, alkali or carbonate supplies the positive metal ion.

questions.stem: Predict the products of the reaction between dilute hydrochloric acid and zinc oxide.
questions.explanation: Zinc oxide is a base, so it neutralises the acid to give a salt and water; hydrochloric acid gives a chloride.

questions.stem: Calcium ions are Ca²⁺ and nitrate ions are NO₃⁻. What is the formula of calcium nitrate?
questions.explanation: Two nitrate ions are needed to balance the 2+ charge on one calcium ion, and the bracket shows that both are nitrate ions.

questions.stem: Zinc ions are Zn²⁺ and sulfate ions are SO₄²⁻. What is the formula of zinc sulfate?
questions.explanation: The 2+ and 2− charges cancel one to one, so no extra subscripts are needed.

questions.stem: (HT) Why is the reaction between zinc and dilute hydrochloric acid described as a redox reaction?

options.text: Zinc gains electrons and hydrogen ions lose them
Zinc atoms lose electrons and hydrogen ions gain them
No oxygen is involved, so it is not a redox change
Hydrogen is released because acids contain hydrogen

questions.explanation: Redox is defined by electron transfer: zinc is oxidised as it loses electrons and the hydrogen ions are reduced as they gain them.

questions.stem: (HT) In the reaction Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂, which species is oxidised?

options.text: Hydrogen ions, as they lose electrons
Chloride ions, as they change place
Magnesium, as it loses two electrons

questions.explanation: Each magnesium atom loses two electrons to form Mg²⁺, and loss of electrons is oxidation.

questions.stem: (HT) Which line shows the reduction step when iron reacts with dilute sulfuric acid, and names it correctly?

options.text: Fe → Fe²⁺ + 2e⁻, the loss of electrons
Fe²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Fe, forming the iron metal

questions.explanation: The hydrogen ions gain electrons to form hydrogen molecules, and gain of electrons is reduction.
